compareCandidate.label: Volume vs. area
compareCandidate.description: Area tiles a flat surface in square units; volume fills a solid in cubic units. Same object viewed flat vs. full.

plainLanguageExplanation: Volume is how much space a 3D object takes up, measured in cubic units — little unit cubes that pack the solid. A rectangular prism is a box, and its volume is length × width × height. A box 4 long, 3 wide, and 2 tall holds 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 unit cubes. Think of it as the area of the base layer (length × width) multiplied by how many layers tall the box is (height). Volume answers 'how much water fits?', 'how much dirt fills this hole?', 'how much room is in this box?'

keyFacts.label: Units
keyFacts.value: Cubic units, like cm³ or m³

whyItMatters: Volume measures the space inside everything 3D — the water in a pool, the sand in a bucket, the air in a room. It is the measurement of capacity and fullness.
didYouKnow: The cubic unit you count — a 1-by-1-by-1 cube — is the 3D cousin of the square unit. Just as squares tile a surface, cubes pack a solid, filling three dimensions.
compareReason: Students flatten 3D shapes in their minds — comparing the flat surface with the filled solid shows why cubic units take the extra dimension.
